key_insight: LLM-generated SQL enabled rapid, explicit screening for potential cancer trial eligibility, with 95.8% agreement against physician consensus.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support trial prescreening for advanced cancers, but does not establish definitive eligibility.
method: Collected 746 recruiting US treatment trials for advanced breast, colon, and non-small cell lung cancers.
Converted trial criteria into reusable SQL and 24 synthetic patient vignettes into structured records.
Used rule-based matching without further LLM inference and validated results against physician review.
evidence_signal: Matching agreed with physician consensus on 230/240 patient-trial pairs (83.3% sensitivity; 100% specificity), with a median runtime of 0.459 seconds per patient across 746 trials, excluding patient-data preparation.
watch_item: Evaluation used synthetic patients and omitted laboratory results and comorbidities; missed matches and real-world performance require further validation.
paper_title: Quantifying Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Using Artificial Intelligence-Based Matching
